application_guidance.input_pattern: A finite full-information strategy set with linear mixture loss, fixed interior beta and a normalized prior assigning positive mass to the intended comparator.
read_original_when: Using a subset or infinite-strategy extension.
Optimizing beta or invoking later regret corollaries.
Changing the feedback, sampling actions, or replacing mixture loss with a different metric.
Changing the update rule or handling unbounded losses.
sensitive_conditions: The comparator must have positive initial weight for a finite logarithmic bound.
The protocol reveals all losses after the allocation and charges mixture loss.
beta is fixed in (0,1); endpoints are excluded from this finite formula.

complexity_scope.guarantee: Deterministic, pathwise inequality for every bounded loss sequence, including adaptive sequences.
complexity_scope.hidden_constants: The loss inequality is exact and has no hidden constants. The operation-count O notation is implementation accounting, not part of Equation (7).
complexity_scope.oracle: Full loss-vector feedback after allocation choice, including all N coordinate losses each trial.
complexity_scope.output_and_metric: Sequence of simplex allocations p^t; cumulative linear mixture loss L_H compared with coordinate cumulative loss L_i. No claim about realized sampled-action loss.
complexity_scope.regime: Finite N,T; fixed 0<beta<1; normalized nonnegative prior; positive prior mass on the compared strategy.
complexity_scope.resource: T vector-feedback rounds and NT revealed scalar losses. The displayed implementation uses O(N) scalar arithmetic plus N power evaluations per round and O(N) working storage; precision, power evaluation and generating losses are separately charged implementation resources.
complexity_scope.upper_witness_or_lower_coverage: Upper performance bound for the specified Hedge update. No lower-bound coverage over algorithms is asserted.

evidence.statement_check: Equation (7), all required definitions and standing assumptions, and its complete source argument were checked against original-page images.

content.intended_use: Upper-bound the cumulative mixture loss of the displayed Hedge update relative to a positive-prior strategy.

proofs.full_source_argument: Faithful restatement of the complete source argument needed for Equation (7): let h_t=p^t dot ell^t. Convexity of r -> beta^r on [0,1] bounds it by the chord 1-(1-beta)r. Multiplying this scalar inequality by each nonnegative w_j^t and summing yields W_{t+1}<=W_t(1-(1-beta)h_t). Since W_1=1, iteration and 1-x<=exp(-x) yield W_{T+1}<=exp(-(1-beta)sum_t h_t). The update also yields w_i^{T+1}=w_i^1 beta^{sum_t ell_i^t}; all weights being nonnegative, W_{T+1}>=w_i^1 beta^{L_i}. For w_i^1>0 and beta>0 these bounds are positive and may be logged. Thus ln w_i^1+L_i ln beta <= ln W_{T+1} <= -(1-beta)L_H. Rearrangement using 1-beta>0 proves Equation (7). This is source-linked exposition, not a new local Theorem or a transfer claim.
proofs.locator: PDF/printed p.5 Lemma 1, Equations (3)–(6); p.6 Theorem 2 Proof and Equation (7)
map: Source Lemma 1: convexity gives beta^r <= 1-(1-beta)r for r in [0,1]. Therefore W_{t+1}=sum_j w_j^t beta^{ell_j^t} <= W_t[1-(1-beta)p^t dot ell^t].

Source Lemma 1 continuation: iterate from W_1=1 and apply 1+x<=exp(x), obtaining W_{T+1} <= product_t[1-(1-beta)p^t dot ell^t] <= exp[-(1-beta)L_H]. Hence Equation (5) states L_H <= -ln W_{T+1}/(1-beta).
Source Equation (6): repeated multiplicative updates give w_i^{T+1}=w_i^1 product_t beta^{ell_i^t}=w_i^1 beta^{L_i}.

Source Theorem 2 Proof establishes the subset version using W_{T+1} >= sum_{i in S}w_i^1 beta^{L_i} >= beta^{max_{i in S}L_i}sum_{i in S}w_i^1. The source explicitly identifies Equation (7) as the S={i} case.

For the selected singleton, W_{T+1} >= w_i^1 beta^{L_i}>0. Taking logarithms gives -ln W_{T+1} <= -ln w_i^1-L_i ln beta. Combine with Equation (5), dividing by 1-beta>0, to obtain the recorded conclusion.
proofs.omitted_details: No algebraic step required for the finite singleton bound is intentionally omitted. Lemma 1 and Equation (6) are included inline from the same Source rather than linked to unreviewed external records. The subset extension and later tuned bounds are outside this recorded statement.

assumptions: N and T are positive integers.
Every loss vector ell^t lies in [0,1]^N and is fully revealed after p^t is chosen.
Initial weights are nonnegative and sum to one; for a finite comparison to strategy i require w_i^1>0. Weights of other strategies may be zero.
Allocations and updates are exactly the displayed Figure 1 Hedge rules; incurred loss is the linear mixture loss p^t dot ell^t.
statement.conclusion: L_H <= [-ln(w_i^1) - L_i ln(beta)]/(1-beta), simultaneously for every positive-prior comparator i. This is Theorem 2 Equation (7) in its finite-log regime.
statement.objects_and_definitions: There are N strategies and T trials. Start from w^1 in [0,1]^N with sum_j w_j^1=1. With W_t=sum_j w_j^t, set p_j^t=w_j^t/W_t and w_j^{t+1}=w_j^t beta^{ell_j^t} after receiving ell^t. Define L_H=sum_{t=1}^T sum_j p_j^t ell_j^t and L_i=sum_{t=1}^T ell_i^t. Here ln is the natural logarithm.
statement.parameter_domains: N,T in positive integers; beta in (0,1); w^1 in [0,1]^N with sum_j w_j^1=1; comparator i has w_i^1>0; ell^t in [0,1]^N.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every N,T, every fixed beta in (0,1), every normalized nonnegative initial vector, every sequence ell^1,...,ell^T in [0,1]^N, and every i in {1,...,N} with w_i^1>0, the inequality holds. No stochastic assumption or averaging over the loss sequence is needed. In particular it holds on every sequence generated by an adaptive environment that observes the current allocation.

summary: For every bounded loss sequence, fixed interior beta and positive-prior comparator i, Hedge's cumulative mixture loss is at most (-ln w_i^1-L_i ln beta)/(1-beta).
title: Hedge prior-dependent loss bound: Theorem 2 singleton case
use_when: Compare full-information Hedge mixture loss against a specified strategy with positive prior mass.
Use an exact prior-sensitive loss inequality; do not treat it as a sampled-action tail bound or unrestricted Oracle Complexity statement.
